newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovaks seek to increase exports to Russia.
newsitem.headline: Slovaks seek to increase exports to Russia.

text.p: Slovakia, in an attempt to curb its burgeoning trade deficit, is looking to boost heavy engineering and machinery exports to Russia, Economics Minister Karol Cesnek said on Thursday.

Speaking on state radio after a four-day visit to Moscow, Cesnek said Slovakia currently imports most of its raw materials from Russia, but the few projects operating which could accelerate exports were an insufficient counterbalance.
"We are buying all our basic raw materials, such as coal, iron ore, oil and gas from Russia," Cesnek said.

"But if we are talking about the expansion of projects in the shoe or textile industries, then we should note that there are only tens of millions (crowns) involved. To balance our trade deficit, we need to boost this figure into the billions," he added.
This year's trade gap hit 35.3 billion crowns by the end of August period with a deficit to Russia accounting for 32.23 billion crowns.

In contrast, the shortfall with OECD countries was only 10.83 billion crowns. A trade surplus with most other central european, African and Asian countries managed to keep the deficit from being even larger.
Cesnek, the former general director of energy monopoly Slovenske Elektrarne, named the energy industry and ecological equipment as opportunities for Slovak exports to Russia.

"We need to find whether there are real obstacles, also on our side, preventing our companies from entering the Russian market," he said. "So far we have been missing some measures such as export credits."
He added that the Russians have been expressing interest in creating light industry joint-ventures with the Slovaks, which could also operate in third markets.
Cesnek has also said he supports a project creating a joint Slovak-Russian bank, which has been also called for by Slovak companies already operating in Russia, to provide factoring services.
